subject: Security questionnaire: PII handling, subprocessors, and cross-border flows
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@oligohealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: oligohealth-security@oligohealth.com
Date: 2028-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial SSQ: PII flows, processors + cross-border detail

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. OligoHealth's security team has a few follow-up items we need documented for our DPA review and a short security questionnaire. In particular we need: 1) a dataflow diagram showing where PII is processed (including prefix/KV cache behavior), 2) list of current subprocessors and which country each is hosted in, 3) details on KMS custody for customer keys and whether any key material crosses borders, and 4) RBAC/access roles for teams with PI access (including any shadow or emergency access pathways).

Can you send a consolidated packet we can attach to our procurement file? We're on a tight timeline — procurement needs anything that impacts EU transfer clauses by Friday EOD (our timezone).

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Security Operations
OligoHealth

(attachment: OligoHealth_SSQ_v1.pdf)

From: jordan.blake@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya@oligohealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SSQ: PII flows, processors + cross-border detail

Hi Priya — thanks for the list and the call earlier. We're compiling a single packet for you. Quick notes on timing and owners below:

- Dataflow diagram + short narrative: Marissa (Privacy) will produce the annotated drawio export showing in-region vs cross-border hops, cache behavior (prefix/KV), and where ephemeral copies may be created.
- Subprocessors inventory (current + planned): Ben will attach the canonical CSV and PDF export with country hosting and contract link.
- KMS custody & export: Neha will provide a KMS custody matrix with details on root key locations, any HSM/KMS partners, and whether key material ever leaves region.
- Access roles: I'll include the RBAC mapping and our emergency access workflow (justification, logging, and alerting).

Action: We'll share the packet to your Drive link + the attachments below by EOD tomorrow (2028-05-10). If you need a signed annex or a data transfer supplemental, flag it and I will escalate to Legal.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

(attachments to follow)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-09T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Initial SSQ: PII flows, processors + cross-border detail

Folks — I'm drafting the drawio export and will include two layers: an operational view (clusters, K/V cache, ingest) and a compliance view (where PII is persisted, retention windows, and subprocessors tied to each hop). Notes/questions:

- For prefix/KV caching: include that prefixes are cached with TTLs and that KV snapshots are ephemeral; clarify that persisted data (logs/audits) are stored in region X unless customer opts into cross-region replication.
- For cross-border transfers: we should explicitly call out where fallbacks route (e.g., hot fallback to us-west when eu capacity saturated) and cite routing policy: latency-first for Hosted, region-pin for Private/Dedicated.
- KMS: I'll reference Neha's custody table; need explicit confirmation whether any KMS key material is escrowed with a partner (note: we do not escrow customer private keys by default).

I'll attach redwood_dataflow_v3.drawio.png and the annotated notes when ready. Marissa
Privacy Lead | Redwood Inference

(attachment: redwood_dataflow_v3.drawio.png)

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-09T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SSQ: PII flows, processors + cross-border detail

Attached inventory export (CSV + PDF). Highlights: current subprocessors include: (1) CloudInfra EU (compute + storage) — eu-central; (2) MetricsCloud (telemetry) — us-east; (3) KeyPartner HSM service — eu-west. Planned: an additional caching edge partner in ap-south for performance but not yet active.

I also added a column for contract links and whether each subprocessor processes PII fields vs anonymized telemetry. See subprocessors_inventory_20280509.pdf and kms_custody_matrix.csv.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

(attachments: subprocessors_inventory_20280509.pdf, kms_custody_matrix.csv)

From: Priya Shah <priya@oligohealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: oligohealth-security@oligohealth.com
Date: 2028-05-10T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SSQ: PII flows, processors + cross-border detail

Jordan — received the packet, thanks. A couple of clarifications from our legal/security review: 1) In the dataflow diagram you reference a fallback to us-west — can you confirm whether the eu-to-us fallback creates any persistent backups in the US, or whether routing is ephemeral and only affects live inference paths? 2) For KeyPartner HSM: are audit logs for KMS operations retained in the same region as the HSM or replicated to a central logging service (and if so, where)? 3) Please provide a short statement we can attach to our DPA noting that Redwood will not escrow customer private keys and that emergency access requires a documented approval workflow.

If you can return those three items in a single email, we can mark the questionnaire as satisfied and proceed with procurement.

Best,
Priya
Head of Security Operations
OligoHealth
